issues.legal_issue: A conviction for an individual assault cannot be sustained by reconstructing a prosecution case when the prosecution has not established the true genesis and manner of the occurrence and the evidence leaves a probability of self-defence.
material_facts: The High Court found that the prosecution witnesses’ accounts were inconsistent and that the prosecution had not presented the true version of the occurrence.
People on both sides were injured, including grievous injuries, and the accused had multiple injuries, one of them grievous.
The High Court could not determine how the occurrence began or who was the aggressor, and found that it was not a free fight.
Although the High Court did not accept the defence account, the accused’s injuries made it difficult to exclude the probability that he acted in self-defence.
The High Court nevertheless upheld the accused’s conviction for an individual assault.
issues.conclusion: The conviction and sentence were set aside and the accused was acquitted because the prosecution had not proved its case beyond reasonable doubt, and the court could not sustain the conviction by reconstructing a new case of individual assault.
issues.legal_principle: The prosecution must prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Where the true version and genesis of an occurrence are not established, a court cannot reconstruct a new case to sustain an individual assault; a probability that the accused acted in self-defence is sufficient to entitle the accused to acquittal. The judgment cites no earlier cases or statutory provision as the basis for this principle; Section 304, Part I, IPC is identified only as the provision under which the conviction had been entered.

rule.if: criminal_conviction_appeal and prosecution_version_rejected and injuries_on_both_sides and aggressor_unknown and not_free_fight and self_defence_probable

predicates.criminal_conviction_appeal: An accused appealed a criminal conviction for an individual assault.
predicates.prosecution_version_rejected: The court found that the prosecution had not established the true version, genesis, or manner of the occurrence.
predicates.injuries_on_both_sides: People on both sides of the dispute were injured, including people with grievous injuries.
predicates.aggressor_unknown: The court could not determine how the occurrence began or who was the aggressor.
predicates.not_free_fight: The court found that the occurrence was not a free fight.
predicates.self_defence_probable: The accused’s injuries and the circumstances left a probability that the accused acted in self-defence.

issues.definition: When an accused appeals an individual-assault conviction, the prosecution version is rejected, both sides suffered injuries, the aggressor is unknown, the occurrence was not a free fight, and self-defence is probable, the conviction is set aside and the accused is acquitted.
